concept.name: CelestialBody
concept.definition: A naturally occurring physical body in outer space, such as a planet, star or moon.

provenance.note: Structural root for the domain; the concrete subkinds below are grounded in IAU nomenclature.

property.name: mass
property.definition: The total amount of matter in the body.

provenance.note: A universal property of any celestial body; per-body values are sourced at L2 (NASA NSSDC Planetary Fact Sheet).

property.name: equatorialRadius
property.definition: The radius of the body measured at its equator.

provenance.note: Equatorial (not mean) radius; per-body values are sourced at L2 (NASA NSSDC Planetary Fact Sheet).

invariant.message: A celestial body must have a positive mass.

concept.name: Planet
concept.definition: A celestial body that orbits the Sun, is massive enough for its self-gravity to pull it into a nearly round shape, and has cleared the neighbourhood around its orbit.

provenance.source: IAU 2006 General Assembly, Resolution B5: Definition of a Planet in the Solar System

property.name: orbitalPeriod
property.definition: The time the planet takes to complete one orbit around the Sun (its sidereal period).

provenance.note: Per-planet values are sourced at L2 (NASA NSSDC Planetary Fact Sheet, orbital period in days).

property.name: numberOfMoons
property.definition: The number of confirmed natural satellites in orbit around the planet.

provenance.note: Per-planet counts are sourced at L2 (NASA NSSDC Planetary Fact Sheet) and revised as new satellites are confirmed by the IAU Minor Planet Center.

invariant.message: A planet cannot have a negative number of moons.

concept.name: DwarfPlanet
concept.definition: A celestial body that orbits the Sun and is nearly round, but has NOT cleared the neighbourhood around its orbit and is not a satellite.

provenance.source: IAU 2006 General Assembly, Resolution B5: Definition of a Planet in the Solar System

concept.name: Star
concept.definition: A celestial body that shines by its own light through sustained nuclear fusion in its core.

provenance.note: Standard astronomical usage; included as a sibling subkind (e.g. the Sun of the Solar System).

concept.name: NaturalSatellite
concept.definition: A celestial body in orbit around a planet or other non-stellar body (a moon).

provenance.note: Standard astronomical usage; 'moon' is the common synonym.

concept.name: PlanetarySystem
concept.definition: A collection of celestial bodies — a star (or stars) together with the planets, dwarf planets and smaller bodies gravitationally bound to it.

provenance.note: A Collection: its members are joined by the part_of relation declared on CelestialBody, not by inheritance.

property.name: numberOfPlanets
property.definition: The number of bodies in the system classified as planets.

provenance.note: Per-system values are sourced at L2 (for the Solar System, the count of 8 follows IAU 2006 Resolution B5).

individual.name: Mercury
individual.definition: The smallest planet and the closest to the Sun.

provenance.ref: Mercury: mass, equatorial radius, orbital period, number of moons

individual.name: Venus
individual.definition: The second planet from the Sun and the hottest in the Solar System.

provenance.ref: Venus: mass, equatorial radius, orbital period, number of moons

individual.name: Earth
individual.definition: The third planet from the Sun and the only known body to support life.

provenance.ref: Earth: mass, equatorial radius, orbital period, number of moons

individual.name: Mars
individual.definition: The fourth planet from the Sun, a cold desert world often called the Red Planet.

provenance.ref: Mars: mass, equatorial radius, orbital period, number of moons

individual.name: Jupiter
individual.definition: The fifth and largest planet in the Solar System, a gas giant.

provenance.ref: Jupiter: mass, equatorial radius, orbital period, number of moons

individual.name: Saturn
individual.definition: The sixth planet from the Sun, a gas giant famous for its ring system.

provenance.ref: Saturn: mass, equatorial radius, orbital period, number of moons

individual.name: Uranus
individual.definition: The seventh planet from the Sun, an ice giant that rotates on its side.

provenance.ref: Uranus: mass, equatorial radius, orbital period, number of moons

individual.name: Neptune
individual.definition: The eighth and most distant planet from the Sun, an ice giant.

provenance.ref: Neptune: mass, equatorial radius, orbital period, number of moons

individual.name: Pluto
individual.definition: A dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt. Classified as the ninth planet from 1930 until 2006, when the IAU adopted the planet/dwarf-planet distinction; Pluto shares its orbital neighbourhood with other Kuiper-belt objects and so is a dwarf planet, not a planet. It has five known moons and an orbital period of about 90,560 days.

provenance.source: IAU 2006 General Assembly, Resolution B6: Pluto
provenance.ref: Resolution B6 (Pluto is a dwarf planet by the Resolution B5 definition and the prototype of a new category of trans-Neptunian objects); B5 itself does not name Pluto

individual.name: Solar System
individual.definition: The planetary system of the Sun, containing the eight planets, the dwarf planets and smaller bodies bound to it.

provenance.source: IAU 2006 General Assembly, Resolution B5: Definition of a Planet in the Solar System
provenance.ref: Resolution B5 (footnote 1 enumerates the eight planets; the definition excludes Pluto, which Resolution B6 classes as a dwarf planet)
